summary: Built an Ansible playbook on node1 that creates a "Fleet Internal CA" (self-signed openssl CA), issues a TLS certificate for node2 (CN=node2, SAN DNS:node2/IP:10.100.196.11), deploys nginx on node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 with that certificate, and installs the CA into the system trust store on both node1 and node2. Verified end-to-end with an openssl chain verify and a curl request to https://node2:8443 that validated successfully against the system CA trust store. Also fixed a pre-existing broken sshd on node2 (missing host keys, missing /run/sshd, service disabled) so Ansible could reach it over SSH. Completed the mandatory sequential restart-and-recovery protocol on all three nodes with boot-id proof of restart and post-restart health verification.
actions_performed: Installed ansible and sshpass on node1 (the control node) via apt
Set up cluster SSH keys and /etc/hosts on node1 and node2 for Ansible connectivity
Diagnosed and fixed broken sshd on node2: generated missing host keys, created /run/sshd, added a tmpfiles.d rule for persistence across boots, enabled and started ssh.service
Wrote Ansible inventory.ini and playbook.yml at /root/ansible/fleet-ca on node1

Playbook play 1 (hosts: node1/local): creates CA directory structure, generates CA private key and self-signed 'Fleet Internal CA' certificate, generates node2 key/CSR/signed certificate with SAN, installs the CA into node1's system trust store via update-ca-certificates

Playbook play 2 (hosts: node2): installs nginx, copies node2 key/cert/CA cert from the controller, configures an nginx site listening on 0.0.0.0:8443 with ssl_certificate/ssl_certificate_key, installs the CA into node2's system trust store, ensures nginx is enabled and started
Ran ansible-playbook (syntax-check then full apply): all tasks ok/changed, 0 failed

Verified CA cert subject/issuer, node2 cert SAN and CA signature via openssl verify, and the HTTPS 8443 endpoint via curl from node1 (validated against system trust store) and node2 (localhost curl with cacert)

Captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, service state) on all three nodes, then sequentially rebooted node1, node2, and node3, polling each until reachable and confirming a changed boot_id as restart proof, and re-verified CA/cert files, system trust store, and nginx/8443 health after each restart

evidence.requirement: Fleet Internal CA created on node1
evidence.summary: Ansible run generated the CA key/cert on node1; openssl x509 shows subject=CN=Fleet Internal CA, issuer=CN=Fleet Internal CA (self-signed)

evidence.requirement: TLS certificate issued for node2 by the CA
evidence.summary: node2.crt has subject=CN=node2, issuer=CN=Fleet Internal CA, SAN DNS:node2/IP:10.100.196.11; openssl verify against ca.crt returns OK

evidence.requirement: node2 serves HTTPS on port 8443 with the issued certificate
evidence.summary: ss shows nginx listening on 0.0.0.0:8443; curl from node1 with --resolve completed a TLS 1.3 handshake showing 'SSL certificate verify ok' and matching SAN; curl from node2 using the system CA bundle got HTTP=200

evidence.requirement: CA installed as trusted system CA on node1
evidence.summary: update-ca-certificates ran (changed) on node1; /etc/ssl/certs shows fleet-internal-ca.pem symlink and hash link c9601fe1.0

evidence.requirement: CA installed as trusted system CA on node2
evidence.summary: update-ca-certificates ran (changed) on node2; /etc/ssl/certs shows fleet-internal-ca.pem symlink and hash link c9601fe1.0
ansible-core 2.16.3 installed on node1; playbook.yml passed --syntax-check and executed both plays successfully against inventory (ca group=node1 local, web group=node2 ssh)
